summary: Backend-only verification that the JSONB double-encoding fixes applied after iteration_74 make ALL future writes sound. ALL 24 new tests pass. Regressions: test_idor_sec001.py 17/17 pass; test_jsonb_fix_iter74.py 19/20 (the single failure is the legacy 109 corrupted standards_entries.keywords rows the user asked NOT to repair); test_remaining_jsonb_iter74.py now 3/3 (was 2 failing) after updating its legacy-data sweep to informational. Backend restarted: seed ran clean, AWIF Wales keywords/sub_outcomes/key_questions remain jsonb_typeof='array' (repair path did not re-corrupt). Also verified `grep json.dumps` finds ZERO remaining occurrences in routers/ and utils/ (except one comment in seed.py).

minor.issue: 109 legacy rows still jsonb_typeof='string' — types ci(18), ciw(23), niscc_code(12), niscc_induction(7), rqia_dom(16), rqia_res(15), scw(12), sssc(6). These are NOT disposable meeting test data: they are the seeded reference standards used for Wales/Scotland/NI keyword matching. New writes are correct (POST /admin/standards verified array; utils/seed._insert_standards_entries fixed) but the seed is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so these rows will never self-heal in this environment. Runtime survives only because _parse_std_row/_jlist decodes one level. Recommend a one-off idempotent backfill (UPDATE ... SET keywords = keywords #>> '{}' ::jsonb WHERE jsonb_typeof(keywords)='string') for these + any other system-standard jsonb columns.

2 pre-fix rows (c20802af-17e3-4210-b497-13d09c9e67ec, 2f1cc088-0687-48b9-9f40-1dabb5285640) still contain stringified array ELEMENTS. Left as-is per explicit user instruction; noted because jsonb_typeof-based checks cannot detect this class, so any future migration must validate element-level.

Robustness only (no live bug found): _jdict decodes exactly one level, so a triple-encoded value yields a str and `branding["primary_color"]=...` raises TypeError → HTTP 500. I hit this transiently after my own test teardown mistakenly re-encoded the value; a legacy double-encoded value is handled fine (verified by test_put_branding_survives_legacy_double_encoded_value, passing). Consider a while-isinstance(str) loop in _jdict/_jlist for defence in depth.

Still open from iteration 74 (not re-tested this pass): outputs are not passed through _sanitise_analysis/_apply_uk_language and analyze_custom_only's system prompt has no UK-language ('caseload') rule.
Still slow (login via get_tokens.py takes 8-25s, and hot-reload windows produce transient 502s from the ingress). OTP email send still appears to be on the request path.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Repro commands: cd /app/backend && python3 tests/clear_rate_limit.py && python3 -m pytest tests/test_jsonb_iter75.py -q -n 0 -p no:randomly (~70s, needs backgrounding) and python3 -m pytest tests/test_pipeline_jsonb_iter75.py -q -n 0 (~18s, runs in-process with its own asyncpg pool, no HTTP). _iter75_helpers.db() deliberately registers NO jsonb codec — snapshot/restore uses ::text so it cannot double-encode (my first version DID register the codec and corrupted organisations.branding into a triple-encoded string, repaired with tests/fix_branding_iter75.py --fix; do not re-add the codec). tests/check_awif_iter75.py and tests/check_residue_iter75.py are quick standalone DB probes. Writing files under /app/backend triggers uvicorn hot reload → transient 502s for ~15s; wait before running API suites.
rca_of_the_issue: asyncpg's jsonb codec (database._init_connection, encoder=json.dumps) means any json.dumps() before a $N::jsonb bind encodes twice. The developer's follow-up removed every remaining occurrence in routers/ and utils/ (grep now returns 0 code hits), including the `||` concat sites in recording.py where the corruption was element-level and invisible to jsonb_typeof, and the seed.py AWIF repair path that was itself re-encoding. All of those paths are now verified sound for new writes by live API and in-process pipeline tests. The only remaining artefacts are pre-existing corrupted rows (109 standards_entries.keywords + 2 meetings.recording_events + 3 transcripts.safety_warnings-era rows), which the user explicitly declined to repair.
